{"id": "40:28/q09", "question": "How does min āli Firʿawn attach?", "turns_on": "Whether min āli Firʿawn modifies the man or is advanced from the object of 'conceals'; the construction of katama and word order decide.", "positions": [{"id": "40:28/q09/p1", "position": "The phrase describes the man as from Pharaoh's household", "reasons": "RAZI-FULL, d. 606 (قيل): A reported parse attaches “min” to “conceals his faith,” but an objection says Arabic does not express concealing something from someone in this construction; 4:42 is cited. | mentions 4:42 RAZI-FULL, d. 606: A second objection says that if this reasoning were sound, every liar could use it to defend a false religion. {"id": "40:28/q10", "question": "Why are the man's descriptions ordered this way?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "40:28/q10/p1", "position": "Faith and affiliation precede the concealing clause", "reasons": "BURHAN, d. 794: The examples place nominal material, a prepositional phrase, and a verbal clause in sequence; the adverbial form belongs between them because it resembles both noun and clause. {"id": "40:28/q11", "question": "Why and how did he conceal or disclose his faith?", "turns_on": "Whether concealment lasted until danger to Moses and whether the reported hundred years is accepted.", "positions": [{"id": "40:28/q11/p1", "position": "He concealed faith for safety or effective counsel", "reasons": "BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 (قوم): Some say the believing man was an Israelite, with min āli Firʿawn understood as describing whom he concealed his faith from. IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 (أبو الفضل الجوهري): In a sermon on the Companions’ merits, Abu al-Fadl al-Jawhari cited God’s preservation of the concealed believer’s speech in scripture and argued that the Prophet’s Companions deserved still greater honor. IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 (الحسن): Al-Hasan says the man believed before Moses came, as did Pharaoh's wife.
